extraction.name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
extraction.description: A benchmark for text embeddings spanning 8 embedding tasks, 58 datasets, and 112 languages, with open-source software and a public leaderboard.
extraction.creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers
extraction.citeAs: Muennighoff, Niklas; Tazi, Nouamane; Magne, Loïc; Reimers, Nils. 2023. MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. arXiv:2210.07316v3.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MTEB aggregates datasets from multiple existing benchmarks and sources, and also creates custom datasets for MTEB using public APIs and available platform data. New datasets can be added by specifying a Hugging Face dataset name where the data has been uploaded.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web API, Document analysis, User-generated content data, Others
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include SemEval datasets, BEIR datasets, Hugging Face datasets, public APIs from arXiv and bioRxiv/medRxiv, Reddit posts, StackExchange posts, and datasets hosted on Kaggle and other public repositories.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: 2003-01-01 to 2018-12-31 for the MedrxivClusteringP2P example dataset; otherwise not specified benchmark-wide.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For clustering datasets, MTEB creates sentence-to-sentence and paragraph-to-paragraph variants; for P2P settings titles are concatenated with abstracts or post bodies. For arXiv, only the first category is used when multiple categories are assigned. Subsets of labels are selected and articles sampled to create splits with varying cluster sizes.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Texts are organized into sentence-to-sentence, paragraph-to-paragraph, and sentence-to-paragraph categories. In some clustering tasks, titles alone are used for S2S while title plus content/abstract are concatenated for P2P. Models may truncate inputs if necessary.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations come from original source datasets and human-provided labels such as translations, intents, sentiments, toxicity, paraphrase labels, similarity scores, relevance judgments, and summarization assessments. For custom clustering datasets, labels are generated from categories assigned to papers by humans.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark emphasizes reproducibility through dataset and software versioning; JSON result files are released, and the benchmark is maintained through community pull requests and leaderboard submissions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to make selecting the right embedding model easier and simplify future embedding research and industry application decisions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: MTEB average scores are biased toward tasks with many datasets, especially retrieval, classification, and clustering. Results may also be affected by overlap between benchmark datasets and model training data, but the benchmark does not control for this contamination.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include missing very long document datasets, task imbalance with summarization underrepresented, limited multilingual coverage for retrieval and clustering, lack of code datasets, and exclusion of additional modalities beyond natural language.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluation of text embedding models across bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity, and summarization; evaluation is performed mainly on test splits, except MSMARCO where the dev split is used.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: For S2S datasets, the input text is simply the title of the paper, while for P2P the input text is the concatenation of the title and the abstract. ... for arXiv multiple categories can be given to a single paper so we only use the first one. ... For every dataset, split and strategy, we select subsets of all labels and then sample articles from those labels. This yields splits with a varying amount and size of clusters.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: All datasets are grouped into three categories: Sentence to sentence (S2S) ... Paragraph to paragraph (P2P) ... Sentence to paragraph (S2P) ... MTEB imposes no limit on the input length, leaving it up to the models to truncate if necessary. Several clustering tasks are framed as both S2S and P2P tasks. The former only compare titles, while the latter include both title and content. For ArxivClustering, for example, abstracts are concatenated to the title in the P2P setting.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: The cluster labels are generated using categories given to the papers by humans. ... AmazonCounterfactual ... annotated for counterfactual detection ... AmazonPolarity ... the label is either "positive" or "negative". ... MassiveIntent ... annotated with the associated intent. ... BUCC provides big set of sentences ... along with associated pairs annotation. The annotated pairs here corresponds to a pairs of translated sentences ... SummEval ... alongside human annotations.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: This means MTEB average scores, which are computed over all datasets, are biased towards tasks with many datasets, notably retrieval, classification and clustering. ... Our scale of experiments and that of model pre-training make controlling for data contamination challenging. Thus, we ignore overlap of MTEB datasets with model training datasets in MTEB scores.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: While MTEB aims to be a diverse benchmark to provide holistic performance reviews, the benchmark has its limitations. We list them here: 1. Long document datasets ... 2. Task imbalance ... 3. Multinguality ... However, retrieval and clustering are English-only. ... Further, MTEB does not contain any code datasets ... 4. Additional modalities ... We have focused solely on natural language applications

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) aims to provide clarity on how models perform on a variety of embedding tasks ... MTEB consists of 58 datasets covering 112 languages from 8 embedding tasks: Bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, STS and summarization. ... We evaluate on the test splits of all datasets except for MSMARCO, where the dev split is used
